hints: Focus on what dilute sulfuric acid actually does, it causes acidic hydrolysis by adding water across a bond.
Identify each skeleton first: 1 is propanal, 2 is ethyl propanoate, 3 is propanenitrile, 4 is propyl ethanoate.
Ask yourself which hydrolysis splits to release a 3-carbon acid fragment, the acyl side of an ester or the carbon of a nitrile.
walkthrough:
**Name the four skeletons**

Look carefully at the functional groups, not just the zig-zags. Counting carbons gives you the key.

$1: \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ (propanal, an aldehyde)

$2: \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (ethyl propanoate, an ester)

$3: \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ (propanenitrile, a nitrile)

$4: \text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (propyl ethanoate, an ester)

**Recall acidic hydrolysis reactions**

Dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ heated means water adds with $\text{H}^+$ as catalyst. Two groups do this usefully here.

Ester + water:
$$\text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH}$$

Nitrile + water (in two stages, vigorous heating):
$$\text{RCN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{NH}_3 \text{(as } \text{NH}_4^+ \text{ in acid)}$$

Aldehydes do not hydrolyse like this, they need oxidation to become acids.

**Apply to 2 and 3 to get propanoic acid**

For 2, the acyl part $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO-}$ becomes the acid.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
That acid is propanoic acid, perfect.

For 3, the nitrile carbon becomes the carboxyl carbon.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_3$$
Again you get propanoic acid, so 2 and 3 are the pair.

options.A: Incorrect. 2 does give propanoic acid by acidic ester hydrolysis, but 1 is propanal. An aldehyde is not hydrolysed by dilute acid to a carboxylic acid, it would need a strong oxidising agent.
options.B: Incorrect. Neither 1 nor 4 gives propanoic acid. 1 is propanal which does not hydrolyse, and 4 is propyl ethanoate which hydrolyses to ethanoic acid plus propan-1-ol.
options.C: Correct. 2 is ethyl propanoate and hydrolyses to propanoic acid and ethanol. 3 is propanenitrile and hydrolyses to propanoic acid and ammonium ions. Both separately give propanoic acid.
options.D: Incorrect. 3 does give propanoic acid, but 4 does not. 4 is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOPr}$, so its acyl group has only 2 carbons and hydrolysis gives ethanoic acid, not propanoic acid.
